miniProject.title: Measured scaling predictions and a bounded budget decision
miniProject.brief: Extend `lmlab` with a small measured scaling and mixture study using the reliable trainer, existing decoder family and corpus. Reserve configurations before fitting, test predictions rather than importing published exponents, and choose the next experiment from uncertainty and all-attempt cost on your GPU or CPU.
steps: Build `scaling/`'s fixed-token and fixed-compute planner using the tested decoder. Before training, check parameter conventions, output-head and attention FLOPs, masks and token denominators against analytical counts and tensor inventories; retain unique/processed-token definitions, memory predictions, omitted costs and study-wide budget caps.

Pass TensorTonic's Fit a Data Power Law with a Noise Floor and compare its prescribed fitter with raw nonlinear and no-floor fits on constructed truth. Check analytical allocation against numerical minimization and reject unsupported frontier minima; retain convergence diagnostics and full-precision fits.

Pilot runtime and peak memory, then freeze a capacity-by-exposure matrix with a matched-compute pair, repeated fitting cells and reserved configuration. Train terminal runs independently under fixed tokenizer, evaluation and tuning contracts across paired seeds; audit identifiability and commit the reserved prediction before its run.

Reuse the muP worksheet for measured initialization and early-update coordinate checks across widths and seeds; pass TensorTonic's Diagnose muP Width Invariants. Compare learning-rate-by-batch sweeps and transferred versus neighboring rates at matched tokens and tuning budgets; retain actual updates, warmup exposure and unreached targets.

Fit domain response curves from realized proportions of your existing source corpora; freeze and test an excluded proportion with uncertainty. At matched processed tokens, compare repeated subsets with fresh data and filtered data with unique-token-matched random subsets; retain domain losses, exposure and prediction errors.

Run a CPU recursive-fit diagnostic against fresh sampling, declaring variance conventions. Cross unchanged/annealed schedules and original/synthetic data from the smallest complete decoder checkpoint at matched tokens across paired seeds. Use licensed or decoder-generated text; retain general-domain loss, provenance, overlap/diversity audits and pilot-capped generation/continuation costs.

Measure the reserved error against the frozen rule; retain residual and influence plots, floor/objective sensitivity, declared resampling units and failed regimes. Regenerate evidence from all study records, audit confounds and recommend capacity, tokens, mixture or replication with uncertainty, boundaries and a decisive next experiment.
deliverables: The `scaling/` planner, measured run matrix, fit implementations and committed held-out predictions linked to `registry/`.
Residual, influence, uncertainty, width-transfer, mixture, repetition and synthetic-continuation evidence with all attempts and costs retained.
Clean evidence-regeneration transcript and skeptical budget decision with supported range, negative regime and next decisive experiment.

checks.name: TensorTonic: Fit a Data Power Law with a Noise Floor
checks.note: Pass the prescribed candidate-floor procedure; keep raw nonlinear fits and constructed-truth checks as separate implementations.

checks.name: TensorTonic: Diagnose muP Width Invariants
checks.note: Pass supplied-array cases; measured decoder coordinates and held-out rate-transfer comparisons must supply the actual evidence.

rubric.pass: Your count and fitting oracles pass before training. Measured independent terminal runs conserve declared budgets; repeated cells quantify seed variation, identifiability is audited and reserved predictions precede their runs.
rubric.strong: An ill-conditioned surface triggers a simpler identifiable question rather than precise unsupported exponents; held-out misses remain in the evidence.

rubric.pass: Residual and influence checks retain valid high-loss and unfinished attempts distinctly. Declared resampling units support conditional uncertainty; measured transfer, held-out mixtures, repetition controls and schedule/data continuations isolate their stated contrasts.
rubric.strong: The CPU recursive diagnostic separates estimator bias from path behavior, while general-domain loss and synthetic provenance bound decoder-level conclusions without asserting inevitable collapse.

rubric.pass: Clean regeneration rebuilds tables from immutable records. The all-attempt ledger includes pilots, tuning, generation, retries and evaluation; the decision names uncertainty, confounds, a retained failure regime and the next falsifying experiment.
rubric.strong: Plausible fits reverse an allocation, so the learner chooses an informative replication instead; an independent baseline rerun confirms the strongest supported conclusion.

miniProject.feedsInto: Measured resource contracts, held-out prediction errors and mixture decisions feed adaptation and real-code integration. Frozen evaluator and tokenizer identities, negative regimes and all-attempt accounting become the capstone's allocation and uncertainty evidence.
